title: For a smooth quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal the two intersection products agree after tensoring with the rationals
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a field k and a smooth scheme X over k which is quasi-compact and has affine diagonal, the lemma asserts that the intersection product on CH^*(X) constructed in the regular section agrees, after tensoring with Q, with the one constructed in the smooth section (statement lines 14586-14593). The proof takes alpha in CH^i(X) and beta in CH^j(X), writes both as chern characters capped against [X] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect(X)) otimes Q as in the regular section, sets c = ch(alpha') and c' = ch(beta'), and observes that the regular intersection product produces c cap c' cap [X] (proof lines 14595-14603). This is the same as alpha . beta by Lemma labelled lemma-identify-chow-for-smooth, or rather by the obvious generalisation of that lemma to smooth schemes that are not assumed equidimensional, namely that c -> c cap [X] is an isomorphism; the author notes the generalisation explicitly in the proof (proof lines 14604-14606). Recognising that both products are computed as caps of Chern characters against the fundamental class, with the identification supplied by the bivariant-to-homology isomorphism, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the invoked generalisation is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.
